L24: # S&P 500 earnings calendar: who reports from 9 to 15 November

L117: ## What "estimated" means
L118: 
L119: An estimated date has not been announced by the company: this site computes it by adding 364 days to the date the company announced that same quarter last year. Measured over the 36,671 announcement–report pairs in the SEC archive since 2012, that rule gets the exact day right 47.3% of the time and puts the company in the right week 70.4%.
L120: Put the other way round: 3 in every 10 estimates land in the wrong week, and when they miss they run early more often than late (one week early 21.1% of the time, one week late 5.3%). Within ±1 week they land 96.8%. The median error is 1 day.
L121: That is why an estimated date is published by week and not as a promise of a day, and why it carries its label in its own column. As soon as the company announces the day —or its 8-K reaches EDGAR— the row becomes confirmed and the estimate disappears. On each company's own page nothing is estimated: there you only find events that already happened and dates the company itself announced.
L122: Estimates are only published for companies with at least 8 announcements since 2015 and a median error of 3 days or less. For the rest, nothing is estimated. Today that is 24: BLDR, BLK, CEG, CRH, DPZ, EBAY, FE, FERG, GEV, HOOD, NCLH, PSKY, Q, RCL, RDDT, RSG, RVTY, SATS, SNDK, SOLV, STX, SW, SWKS, WELL.
L123: ## What "confirmed" means
L124: 
L125: Confirmed means one of two things: the company has published the date and it is in the public Nasdaq calendar, or its 8-K with item 2.02 is already in EDGAR and the link to the filing is here. The time is the filing's EDGAR acceptance time in New York: it is an upper bound, because the press release goes out first. And an announced date is a scheduled date: companies do move them.
L126: A company's identity is its SEC CIK, never its symbol. The announcements file stores the symbol EDGAR had on the filing day (GOOG for GOOGL, NWS for NWSA, ANTM for ELV), so matching by symbol would drop 27 of the index's 503 companies, Alphabet and Meta among them. Here the match is by CIK.
L127: The five scores on each row —multifactor, momentum, value, quality and growth— run from 0 to 10 and are those of the ranking the day BEFORE the company reports, which is the figure almost nobody puts next to an earnings date. They come from the same file that paints this site's ranking.
